title: Cordless stick vacuum: safe teardown
summary: A cordless stick vacuum gives a lithium-ion pack (18650 cells in the Dyson V6), a motor with its wiring, a motorised floor head and filters (washable on the Dyson V8). Take the pack off first. It clips or screws into the handle, and while it is on, the motor and brush bar can start at a touch of the trigger or button.

steps.text: If it is on a charger or dock, pull the plug from the wall first. Before you charge it or open it, look at the pack and handle outdoors: swelling, cracks, scorch marks, melted plastic, leaks, heat or a sweet chemical smell. If you find any of these, don't charge it: follow safety_swollen_lithium. Treat a pack that is swollen, leaking, hot or damaged as unusable: no charging and no running (iFixit V6 SV04). If it looks sound and you want to test it, charge it on stone or a metal tray, watched, and unplug it if it warms.
steps.warn: Recalled or warned-about packs and vacuums include the BISSELL Multi Reach (CPSC 24-107), INSE S6P Pro and S6T (CPSC 25-213) and ZAUTNKN replacement packs for Dyson V6 vacuums (CPSC 24-054). Never charge or use these.

steps.text: Unplug the charger from the wall and from the vacuum. Keep your fingers off the trigger or power button from now on (iFixit V6 SV04, Dyson V8 Cyclone manual).

Take the pack off before anything else. Click-in packs, such as the Dyson V8 Cyclone's: press the release button on the handle and slide the pack off (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual). Screwed-in packs, such as the Dyson V6 and V8: take the bin off to reach the screws, undo the two or three screws (at the base and at the back of the handle), and pull the pack down out of the handle (iFixit V8 SV10, iFixit V8 Animal, iFixit V6 SV04).
steps.warn: Keep metal tools off the pack's contacts so nothing bridges them (iFixit V6 SV04). Tape over the contacts as soon as the pack is off.

steps.text: Shark Rocket IX141: slide the handle base off the stick, undo the four screws on the battery cover, and lift the cover off with a plastic pick, then lift the pack out (iFixit Shark IX141).
steps.warn: The cover can take a lot of force to pop off (iFixit Shark IX141). Use plastic tools only, keep your face away, never lever against the pack itself, and stop if the cover won't pop off.

steps.text: Look at the pack now it is off. Swollen, dented, leaking, hot or smelly means stop and follow safety_swollen_lithium. If it is sound, tape its contacts and keep it whole for now.

Outdoors, with a dust mask on, empty the bin inside a dust-proof bag and seal it (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual). Take out the filters: on the V8 Cyclone the pre-filter lifts out of the top of the cyclone and the post-filter twists off anticlockwise (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual).

Take the floor head off the wand. Release the brush bar's end cap and slide the brush bar out (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual). Motorised heads contain electronic components (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual). Where the head has its own motor, undo the head's screws and unplug or cut the motor leads.
steps.warn: Only touch the brush bar with the pack off. With the pack on, a press of the button can spin it and trap fingers.

steps.text: Open the main body: with the pack and bin off, undo the screws on the back of the body and under the middle, then pull the body and motor assembly apart. The Dyson V10 has four on the back and two in front of the handle (iFixit V10 motor).

Lift out the motor with its wiring and any control board, all together, since a brushless motor needs its own board to run. Count the thick leads: three usually means brushless, two usually means a plain DC motor. Models differ, so check yours.
Take the trigger or power switch and its wiring from the handle. On the Dyson V6 the switch is built into the pack, not the handle.

Only if the pack won't hold a charge, shows no swelling, heat or smell, and you want its cells: open its case where there are screws, using plastic tools at any seam, and stop if it is glued or welded shut. Cut the leads from the board one at a time, taping each, then separate the cells as in teardown_laptop_battery.
steps.warn: Never push a blade or screwdriver into a pack seam. iFixit advises against opening a pack unless you are trained for cell-level work (iFixit V6 SV04). Keep any heat under 54 °C (130 °F). Cut one lead at a time: cutters across two can short them. Take off rings and watches.

steps.text: Keep the charger with its pack. Don't open it: it is a mains supply.

Store the pack part-charged, contacts taped, in a metal box of dry sand with a loose lid, away from where people sleep. Check it often for heat or swelling (OSHA SHIB 06-20-2019, safety_swollen_lithium).

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **Battery pack.** A lithium-ion pack. The Dyson V6 (SV04) pack holds 18650 cells (iFixit V6 SV04); the Dyson V8 (SV10) and Shark IX141 guides call theirs lithium-ion (iFixit V8 SV10, iFixit Shark IX141). The one aftermarket V8 pack iFixit lists is rated 21.6 V, 3000 mAh (iFixit Dyson V8 battery). That is a seller's figure for one third-party pack, not a Dyson rating, so read the label on yours and measure it. A pack rated that way is probably six lithium-ion cells in series, which would read about 25.2 V when full. Use it whole with its own board: through a fuse and a DC-DC converter whose input rating is well above the pack's full voltage (30 V or more for a pack like this), it can run LED lights, a radio or USB chargers. Measure the full-charge voltage before you connect anything. If the cells turn out to be 18650s, they can be rebuilt into smaller packs (build_18650_pack).
- **Motor and control board.** A small motor with its fan. Keep the motor, its board and the trigger together. Run from the pack they should still give strong suction, for a small blower or dust extraction. Don't pull hot ash or embers through it. Test it clamped down first.
- **Floor head motor and brush bar.** A small motor and a roller. The motor suits a small fan or a stirrer.
- **Filters.** The Dyson V8 Cyclone's pre- and post-filters are washable. Dyson says to rinse them under a running tap and dry them for at least 24 hours, never near a naked flame (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual). Not a face mask and not a water filter.
- **Charger.** A mains adapter for that pack. Keep it with the pack.
- **Bin and cyclone.** Clear plastic parts, useful as funnels or small containers.

## Variations

- **Click-in packs:** the Dyson V8 Cyclone's pack slides off after you press a release button (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual).
- **Screwed-in packs:** the Dyson V8 (SV10) pack is held by three screws, one at the back of the handle and two at its base under the bin (iFixit V8 SV10). The V8 Animal also has three 18 mm screws, but its guide has you slide the motor away from the handle before you reach them (iFixit V8 Animal). The V6 (SV04) has two screws (iFixit V6 SV04).
- **Handle-base packs:** the Shark Rocket IX141's pack sits behind a four-screw cover on the back of the handle base (iFixit Shark IX141).
- **Body screws:** the Dyson V10's motor assembly separates after nine screws in all, three of them around the battery (iFixit V10 motor).
- **Pack fires:** BISSELL recalled about 142,000 Multi Reach vacuums in 2024 after 17 reports of smoking or burning smells, six with the pack catching fire (CPSC 24-107). CPSC warned in 2025 that INSE S6P Pro and S6T packs can overheat and ignite while charging or in use, with at least 10 fires reported (CPSC 25-213). Cheap replacement packs are a risk too: CPSC warned about ZAUTNKN packs for Dyson V6 vacuums after three fires (CPSC 24-054).

## Brush bar and motor

- Dyson says to disconnect the machine from the charger and keep clear of the power button before you clean the brush bar (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual). Go further: take the pack off before your fingers go near the brush bar or the motor's fan.
- When you bench-run the motor, clamp it down, keep its housing on, and keep your face out of line with the fan.

## Battery safety

- iFixit says opening, puncturing or shorting a pack is only for people trained in cell-level repair, and warns against metal tools bridging its contacts (iFixit V6 SV04). Step 11 is for people who accept that risk.
- Heat above 54 °C (130 °F), dropping, crushing and puncturing all damage lithium cells. Charging below freezing does too (OSHA SHIB 06-20-2019). The V8 Cyclone won't run or charge below 5 °C (41 °F) (Dyson V8 Cyclone manual).
- Don't put recalled packs in household rubbish or shop battery bins; CPSC says so for the recalled BISSELL and INSE packs (CPSC 24-107, CPSC 25-213).

## What to leave

- **Swollen, leaking, damaged or recalled packs.** Store them in sand outdoors (safety_swollen_lithium).
- **Packs that are glued or welded shut.** Use them whole or store them.
- **The inside of the charger.** It is a mains supply.
- **Old dust and mouldy filters.**

## Testing what you got out

- **Pack:** measure DC volts at its contacts, keeping the probe tips apart, and compare with the label. A reading far below the label's voltage means flat or failing cells: don't charge it (see test_lithium_cell).
- **Motor:** test it with its own board and pack, clamped down, in short bursts (see test_motor).
